hints: Find the velocity at $t = 3\text{ s}$ using the constant acceleration $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$ over the first $3\text{ s}$.
The total distance in the first $8\text{ s}$ equals the area under the velocity-time graph between $t = 0$ and $t = 8$.
Divide the area into three geometric shapes: a triangle from $t = 0$ to $3$, a trapezium from $t = 3$ to $5$, and a triangle from $t = 5$ to $8$.
Calculate each area and sum them to obtain the total distance.
walkthrough:
Find the velocity at $t = 3\text{ s}$ from the acceleration $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$v(3) = u + at = 0 + 3(3) = 9\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the distance as the sum of areas under the velocity-time graph from $t = 0$ to $t = 8$:
$$\text{Area}_1 (0 \le t \le 3) = \frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 9 = 13.5\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Area}_2 (3 \le t \le 5) = \frac{1}{2}(9 + 7)(5 - 3) = \frac{1}{2}(16)(2) = 16\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Area}_3 (5 \le t \le 8) = \frac{1}{2} \times (8 - 5) \times 7 = \frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 7 = 10.5\text{ m}$$

Sum the three areas to find the total distance travelled:
$$\text{Total distance} = 13.5 + 16 + 10.5 = 40\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Recall that the gradient of a velocity-time graph represents acceleration. Over the interval $0 \le t \le 3$, the particle accelerates from rest ($u = 0$) with constant acceleration $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$v = u + at = 0 + 3 \times 3 = 9\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus the velocity reaches $9\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $t = 3\text{ s}$.

Recall that the distance travelled equals the area under the velocity-time graph. We divide the region between $t = 0$ and $t = 8$ into three simple geometric sections:
1. A triangle from $t = 0$ to $t = 3$ with base $3\text{ s}$ and height $9\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$\text{Area}_1 = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 9 = 13.5\text{ m}$$

2. A trapezium from $t = 3$ to $t = 5$ with parallel vertical heights $9\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $7\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and width $5 - 3 = 2\text{ s}$:
$$\text{Area}_2 = \frac{1}{2}(a + b)h = \frac{1}{2}(9 + 7) \times 2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 16 \times 2 = 16\text{ m}$$

3. A triangle from $t = 5$ to $t = 8$ with base $8 - 5 = 3\text{ s}$ and height $7\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$\text{Area}_3 = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 7 = 10.5\text{ m}$$

Add the three areas together to get the total distance:
$$\text{Distance} = 13.5 + 16 + 10.5 = 40\text{ m}$$

hints: Displacement is the signed area of the velocity-time graph: areas above the $t$-axis are positive, while areas below the $t$-axis are negative.
Express the total displacement at $t = 16\text{ s}$ as the displacement up to $t = 8\text{ s}$ plus the displacement from $t = 8$ to $t = 16$.
The region from $t = 8$ to $t = 16$ is a triangle below the time axis with base $16 - 8 = 8\text{ s}$ and signed height $V$.
Set up the equation $40 + \frac{1}{2}(8)(V) = 32$ and solve for $V$.
walkthrough:
Relate total displacement at $t = 16\text{ s}$ to the displacement during the two phases:
$$s(16) = s(8) + \Delta s_{8 \to 16}$$
$$32 = 40 + \Delta s_{8 \to 16}$$
$$\Delta s_{8 \to 16} = 32 - 40 = -8\text{ m}$$

The motion from $t = 8$ to $t = 16$ forms a triangle below the time axis of base $16 - 8 = 8\text{ s}$ and signed height $V$:
$$\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times V = -8$$
$$4V = -8$$

Solve for the minimum velocity $V$:
$$V = \frac{-8}{4} = -2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Recall that displacement from a velocity-time graph is represented by signed area: regions above the $t$-axis represent positive displacement, and regions below represent negative displacement.

Use the given net displacement at $t = 16\text{ s}$ to find the change in displacement during the second stage ($t = 8$ to $t = 16$):
$$s(16) = s(8) + \Delta s_{8 \to 16}$$
Substitute $s(16) = 32\text{ m}$ and $s(8) = 40\text{ m}$:
$$32 = 40 + \Delta s_{8 \to 16}$$
Subtract $40$ from both sides:
$$\Delta s_{8 \to 16} = 32 - 40 = -8\text{ m}$$

From the graph, between $t = 8$ and $t = 16$, the velocity is negative and forms a single triangular region with a base duration of:
$$\Delta t = 16 - 8 = 8\text{ s}$$
The vertex corresponds to the minimum velocity $V$. The signed area of this triangle is:
$$\text{Signed Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times V$$
Substitute the base and signed area:
$$\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times V = -8$$
$$4V = -8$$

Divide both sides by $4$:
$$V = \frac{-8}{4} = -2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus the minimum velocity is $-2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
